title: The host daemon owns the machine's GitHub Actions runner pool and reports its free CI slots

story.as_a: the factory running on a fleet machine
story.i_want_to: have one installed daemon that runs headless sessions, owns the GitHub Actions runner pool and reports its free CI slots to loopctl
story.so_that: CI capacity is a reported number in the same place as session capacity, and the pool's code lives and releases with the rest of the factory

rationale: PRD R3: the host daemon 'merges today's loopctl-runner process and the GitHub Actions runner registration' and reports 'free CI and session slots'; R10 moves 'infra's CI runner provisioning' into this repo. Today the pool is a separate 3,441-line supervisor in another repo (/home/mkreyman/workspace/infra/scripts/ci-runner-pool.sh, run by infra-ci-runner-pool.service), which mints single-use JIT runner configs per job (:11-15, mint_jitconfig :2044) and admits jobs by measured load (infra decision 0021); loopctl never sees its slots. US-52.47 gave the report a ci_slots field; this story fills it and brings the pool's code in.

acceptance_criteria.description: infra's scripts/ci-runner-pool.sh, runner-upgrade.sh, runner-deps.sh, ci-runner-limits.sh, ci-job-handback-install.sh, macos/actions-runner-install.sh, systemd/infra-ci-runner-pool.service, their tests under scripts/tests/ and runbooks/ci-runner-setup.md move to runner/ci/ with their git history, and runner/ci/tests/*.sh run green in this repo's CI.

The runner's install script installs runner/ci/systemd/infra-ci-runner-pool.service with ExecStart pointing at the installed release's ci-runner-pool.sh, keeping KillMode=process, its runtime and state directories and its EnvironmentFile /etc/default/infra-ci-runner-pool unchanged.

LoopctlRunner.CiPool runs `ci-runner-pool.sh --check-json` on each status tick with a 5 s timeout and maps it to ci_slots {total: slot count, free: slots in state ok, busy: slots busy or held, paused}; a timeout, a non-JSON answer or a non-null error field yields ci_slots null and one log line naming the reason.

LoopctlRunner.CiPool.pause/0 stops the pool unit through systemctl (running jobs keep going under KillMode=process) and resume/0 starts it; both are idempotent, are reachable as `bin/loopctl_runner rpc 'LoopctlRunner.CiPool.pause()'` and `... resume()`, and the paused state is reported in ci_slots.paused.

CiPool starts the pool only through the unit manager and only when the unit is not already active, so the daemon never runs a second supervisor beside a live unit; it never execs ci-runner-pool.sh in the supervisor mode itself.
With [ci] absent or enabled = false in the daemon config, or on macOS (no pool unit), CiPool runs no check and controls no unit, and the daemon reports ci_slots null.

infra's ryzen-mode.sh and ryzen-model-window.sh pause and resume CI through the daemon's rpc instead of stopping the unit by name, and infra-status.sh reads the pool through the moved script's path; infra keeps no copy of the moved files.

test_cases.name: the moved pool tests run here (CI job)
steps: bash each test script from the repo root in the runner CI job
expected_results: every test exits 0; the log reaches infra's first commit of the file

test_cases.name: the installed unit keeps its process model (bash test)
preconditions: the install script run against a temp root
expected_results: ExecStart under the release's runner/ci; KillMode=process; EnvironmentFile and directories unchanged

test_cases.name: check-json mapped to ci_slots, and every failure (runner unit)
preconditions: CiPool with an injected command runner returning: fixture JSON with slots ok, ok, busy, held, broken; a 6 s sleep; 'not json'; JSON with error set
expected_results: %{total: 5, free: 2, busy: 2, paused: false}; then null three times with the reason logged

test_cases.name: pause, resume and no second supervisor (runner unit)
preconditions: CiPool with an injected unit manager recording calls; unit active
steps: resume() twice with the unit reported active after the first
expected_results: one stop; ci_slots.paused true; one start, none while active; no exec of the script without --check-json

test_cases.name: CI disabled and macOS (runner unit)
preconditions: config without [ci]; config with enabled true and os :darwin
expected_results: null and no command run, both

test_cases.name: infra's callers use the daemon (infra bash tests)
preconditions: infra's scripts/tests/ryzen-mode-test.sh and ryzen-model-window-test.sh with a stub loopctl_runner on PATH
expected_results: the stub receives pause then resume; no systemctl call on the pool unit; the file is absent

technical_notes: Why the daemon owns the unit instead of becoming its parent: the unit runs with KillMode=process so a supervisor restart leaves running jobs alone, and in ci.slice (CPUWeight=20, written by ci-runner-limits.sh :144) so a job yields to the developer (infra decision 0021). A pool started as a child of loopctl-runner.service would join that service's cgroup: a daemon restart would kill every running CI job, and jobs would lose the slice weighting.

History move: the same method release 2 used for runner/ and chg/ (README names table: runner source in this repo); infra's systemd unit and runbook move with the scripts, and infra's own references (ryzen-mode.sh:27,50, ryzen-model-window.sh:47, infra-status.sh:295-357, ci-job-handback-install.sh:186-194) change in an infra PR in this release.

Runner side (runner/): a new LoopctlRunner.CiPool under LoopctlRunner.Application's daemon children (/home/mkreyman/workspace/loopctl-runner/lib/loopctl_runner/application.ex:117), called from the status tick (control.ex:969) that US-52.47's HostReport uses; command execution goes through an injected runner module so tests never call systemctl (CLAUDE.md Dependency Injection).

--check-json's shape is documented in ci-runner-pool.sh's usage (:38-60): host, error, slots[] of {slot, state: ok|busy|held|stranded|broken}, counts. Stranded and broken slots count in total and in neither free nor busy.
JIT config minting keeps the box's GitHub auth (`gh api`, :2058) as today; moving that token to a loopctl-issued secret is R3's 'secrets loopctl issues' and is not done here (non_goals).
non_goals: Rewriting the pool in Elixir: it moves as it is; its admission rules are unchanged.
Per-job scratch and warm snapshots: release 9 (PRD R8).
Issuing the pool's GitHub token from loopctl: a later story; the box's gh auth stays.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.48.3: the pool runs and admits jobs from GitHub whether or not loopctl is reachable; only the report pauses, and placement already skips a daemon whose sample is stale (US-52.47).
failure_modes.state: AC-52.48.2: the pool's slot state stays in its own runtime and state directories on the machine; loopctl holds only the latest reported count, re-sent every tick.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.48.4: pause and resume are idempotent, so a repeated rpc from a ryzen model-window script changes nothing.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.48.3: the check is bounded at 5 s, and a slow check reports ci_slots null rather than delaying the status.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.48.4: the pool is reached on its machine through the daemon's rpc and the unit manager; loopctl reaches the daemon through its socket.

defaults: free = slots in state ok; busy = busy + held.
macOS reports ci_slots null until a pool runs there.
definition_of_done: On beelink after rollout: runner_pool shows ci_slots for beelink matching `runner/ci/ci-runner-pool.sh --check-json` run by hand, and `bin/loopctl_runner rpc 'LoopctlRunner.CiPool.pause()'` leaves a running CI job finishing while no new one starts.
